bib.title: ConvNeXt V2: Co-designing and Scaling ConvNets with Masked Autoencoders

read.skipped: reference list after offset 55771 skimmed only to the arXiv-id level

question: Can masked-autoencoder pre-training be made to work for pure ConvNets (ConvNeXt) by co-designing the framework and the architecture?
hypothesis: Simply combining ConvNeXt with MAE gives subpar results; adding feature competition (GRN) to the architecture alongside a fully convolutional MAE should fix feature collapse and make masked pre-training effective.
contributions: A fully convolutional masked autoencoder (FCMAE) using sparse convolution in the encoder and a single ConvNeXt block decoder
Global Response Normalization (GRN) layer to counter feature collapse
ConvNeXt V2 model family from Atto (3.7M) to Huge (650M), with pre-trained models, reaching 88.9% on ImageNet-1K with public data only

method.summary: FCMAE masks 60% of 32x32 patches, encodes only visible pixels with submanifold sparse convolution in a ConvNeXt encoder, and reconstructs patch-normalised pixels with one ConvNeXt block decoder (MSE on masked patches). ConvNeXt V2 adds GRN after the expansion MLP and drops LayerScale. Models are pre-trained on IN-1K, fine-tuned end-to-end, and transferred to COCO and ADE20K.

limits: Only end-to-end fine-tuning is reported; no linear-probe or frozen-feature evaluation.
No seeds, error bars or significance tests; differences of 0.1 to 0.5 points are single runs.
Huge trails ViT-H MAE on IN-1K alone (86.3 vs 86.9); authors suggest bigger ViTs benefit more from SSL.
Feature collapse is called a 'potential issue', shown by visualisation and cosine distance; no causal test.
Sparse conv libraries are not highly optimised; the efficiency gain depends on framework (authors concede).
ADE20K models start from IN-1K supervised fine-tuned weights, not raw SSL weights.
Pre-training epochs for the small models in Table 14 are not stated.
Main experiments ran on TPU with dense masked conv; the GPU sparse version is a PyTorch reproduction.

terms.definition: Fully Convolutional Masked AutoEncoder: sparse-conv ConvNeXt encoder with a single ConvNeXt block decoder
Global Response Normalization: global L2 aggregation, divisive normalisation across channels, and calibration, with learnable gamma, beta and a residual

lineage.work: Masked autoencoders are scalable vision learners
